records.root_cause: GradReducePipeline.gradient_reduce_preprocessing was passed gbuf.data (the entire buffer) instead of bucket.data (the per-bucket slice). gradient_scaling preprocessing therefore divided every byte of the joint gradient buffer once per bucket, yielding cumulative scaling factor of (1/dp_size)**num_buckets on the affected ranges instead of (1/dp_size). All-reduce/reduce-scatter then communicated wrongly scaled gradients with no shape mismatch.
records.invariant: After gradient_reduce_preprocessing, the magnitude of bucket.data must equal the pre-scaled magnitude divided by gradient_scaling_factor (not by gradient_scaling_factor**num_buckets).

records.title: DistributedDataParallel target_gradient_scaling_factor uses get_data_parallel_world_size without context_parallel, so gradients are over-scaled by cp_size when CP is enabled
records.root_cause: DistributedDataParallel computed target_gradient_scaling_factor = 1.0 / parallel_state.get_data_parallel_world_size() without with_context_parallel=True. With CP enabled the gradient reduction collective spans the dp*cp ranks, so the gradients should be divided by dp_size*cp_size. Only dividing by dp_size leaves a residual factor of cp_size in the parameter updates.
records.invariant: When context_parallel_size > 1, the gradient_scaling_factor used by DDP must be 1 / (data_parallel_world_size * context_parallel_size).

records.title: DSA indexer loss is not divided by num_microbatches in forward_step_calc_loss, so the auxiliary loss gradient is overweighted by a factor of num_microbatches
records.root_cause: forward_step_calc_loss set MTPLossAutoScaler.set_loss_scale(loss_scale / num_microbatches) but DSAIndexerLossAutoScaler was never given a per-microbatch divisor. As a result the DSA indexer auxiliary loss accumulates num_microbatches times into the gradient instead of being averaged, contributing a (num_microbatches)x larger gradient than the main loss.
records.invariant: DSAIndexerLossAutoScaler.loss_scale at backward time must equal loss_scale / num_microbatches when calculate_per_token_loss=False.

records.title: TEGroupedMLP fused-ops backward_dw skips _trigger_wgrad_accumulation_and_reduce_hooks on the original linear modules, so DDP never zeros param.grad and AccumulateGrad double-counts
records.root_cause: _make_fused_ops creates new GroupedLinear instances for the fused FC1/activation/FC2 path. backward_dw was called on the new instances, but DDP had registered the wgrad-accumulate-and-reduce hooks on the ORIGINAL self.linear_fc1/fc2 modules. Hooks therefore never fired, param.grad was not cleared, and AccumulateGrad performed an additional in-place add into main_grad on the next iteration, silently double-counting expert weight gradients.
records.invariant: After every TEGroupedMLP.backward_dw call, _trigger_wgrad_accumulation_and_reduce_hooks must be invoked exactly once on linear_fc1 and once on linear_fc2.

records.title: Interleaved 1F1B forgets to wait on async P2P send before deallocating the source buffer, sending corrupted activations to the next pipeline stage
records.root_cause: forward_backward_pipelining_with_interleaving issued an isend to the next stage and immediately called deallocate_output_tensor without waiting on send_next_wait_handle. Because isend's HtoD copy is asynchronous, the destination buffer on the next rank could end up with whatever value happened to be left in memory by the time the deallocation reuse cycle began. Training continued with subtly corrupted forward activations propagated down the pipeline.
records.invariant: Whenever deallocate_pipeline_outputs=True, every send_next isend handle must have wait() called before deallocate_output_tensor on the same output_tensor.

records.title: prepare_input_tensors_for_wgrad_compute does not enforce all_gathered_input.contiguous(), so wgrad GEMM reads a non-contiguous strided tensor as if it were contiguous
records.root_cause: prepare_input_tensors_for_wgrad_compute only called grad_output.contiguous() and assumed all_gathered_input was already contiguous. Some upstream paths (NeMo SFT QAT inputs, some reshape/transpose chains) hand in a strided tensor, but fused_weight_gradient_mlp_cuda.wgrad_gemm_accum_* indexes the buffer via flat data_ptr arithmetic. The kernel reads the wrong elements yet the tensor metadata looks valid, so the wgrad accumulation produces silently incorrect numbers.
records.invariant: all_gathered_input.is_contiguous() must be True at the entry of prepare_input_tensors_for_wgrad_compute.

records.title: MoE aux loss not scaled by num_tokens in per_token_loss mode
tensor_parallel.checkpoint runs CheckpointFunction during CUDA graph warmup, causing graph capture to record stale recomputed activations
records.root_cause: tensor_parallel.checkpoint always dispatched to CheckpointFunction.apply, even during graph warmup or capture. CheckpointFunction tries to recompute the saved forward inside the graph context, which corrupts the captured graph because random states and saved tensors get rewritten between warmup and capture passes. The result is a captured graph that on replay produces values that do not match the eager reference.
records.invariant: When is_graph_warmup() or is_graph_capturing() is True, tensor_parallel.checkpoint must invoke function(*args) directly without entering CheckpointFunction.apply.

records.title: _CudagraphReplayNode unconditionally copies user_input into cudagraph_input even when the data pointers already match, overwriting in-place results from preceding ops
records.root_cause: When the user_input tensor is the SAME storage as cudagraph_input (data_ptr equality), copy_ amounts to a self-copy that semantically still launches a kernel. In specific reuse patterns the source and destination data pointers were intentionally identical so no copy was needed, but cudagraph_input.copy_(user_input) was always issued and could overwrite a value that another op had just written, especially under certain stream orderings.
records.invariant: cudagraph_input.copy_(user_input) must only be issued when user_input.data_ptr() != cudagraph_input.data_ptr().

records.title: DDP cast cudagraph manager runs warmup steps and shares mempool across virtual pipeline stages, corrupting captured param-cast outputs across VPP
records.root_cause: _ParamAndGradBucketGroup created a CudaGraphManager for copy_params_from_grad_buffer without num_warmup_steps=0, so the cast graph was warmed up before capture. Combined with cuda_graph_use_single_mempool=True and lack of per-VPP stage scoping, multiple VPP stages shared mempool and warmup buffers, so the captured cast graph for one VPP stage could write into another stage's parameter buffer.
records.invariant: DDP cast cudagraphs must be created with num_warmup_steps=0 and tagged with the current vp_stage so that VPP stages do not share captured buffer pools.

records.title: DistributedOptimizer FP32 shard_model_param uses non-detached view, so the parameter shard participates in autograd and accumulates spurious grad_fn
records.root_cause: _build_model_and_main_param_groups built shard_model_param as model_param.view(-1)[range] without .detach(). Unlike the FP16/BF16 branch (which goes through main_param.detach() copies), the FP32 view kept grad_fn alive. As soon as anything autograd-eligible touched the shard, an extra grad chain was created, leading to silently doubled gradient contributions for FP32 parameters and inconsistent state with the FP16/BF16 path.
records.invariant: Every shard_model_param entry created in _build_model_and_main_param_groups must satisfy shard_model_param.requires_grad == False and shard_model_param.grad_fn is None.

records.title: _ParamAndGradBucket builds local param_to_index from naive concatenation, ignoring per-param padding so optimizer reads from misaligned offsets when distributed optimizer pads to data_parallel_world_size
records.root_cause: _ParamAndGradBucket initialized param_to_index by walking params and assigning offset += param.numel(), but the global param_index_map already had per-param padded offsets. The two layouts diverged whenever a param's size was not a multiple of dp_world_size. param_to_index was then used by the distributed optimizer to slice param_data, so the optimizer wrote/read different slices than where the gradients lived.
records.invariant: For every param in bucket, bucket.param_to_index[param] must equal (param_index_map[param][0] - bucket.offset, param_index_map[param][1] - bucket.offset).

records.title: Latent MoE backward_dw never calls fc1_latent_proj/fc2_latent_proj.backward_dw, so gradient for the latent projection weights is silently zero
records.root_cause: MoELayer.backward_dw only invoked self.experts.backward_dw() and (when shared_experts requested) self.shared_experts.backward_dw(). The new latent projection layers fc1_latent_proj/fc2_latent_proj were never asked to compute their weight gradients, so their main_grad stayed at zero across every microbatch. The optimizer happily applied (lr * 0) to those parameters every step, freezing them at their initialization.
records.invariant: When config.moe_latent_size is set, fc1_latent_proj.backward_dw and fc2_latent_proj.backward_dw must each be called once per backward pass through the MoE layer.

records.title: _CudagraphReplayNode treats fp4_enabled as fp8 only, skipping the per-module FP-recipe restoration on FP4 paths so saved scaling factors drift each replay
records.root_cause: _CudagraphReplayNode.forward only checked runner.fp8_enabled when deciding whether to set is_first_microbatch and restore the per-module DelayedScaling recipe. With FP4 active but FP8 inactive, the recipe restore branch was skipped, so each replay used a stale amax history. Every step shifted the FP4 scale away from the target, causing slowly drifting numerics.
records.invariant: If runner.fp4_enabled, the per-module DelayedScaling recipe restoration must execute identically to the runner.fp8_enabled path.

records.title: _CudaGraphRunner enables FP8 capture for keep-mamba-stack-attention-linear-in-bf16 layers, casting frozen-bf16 attention linears into FP8 inside the captured graph
records.root_cause: _CudaGraphRunner.__init__ set self.fp8_enabled = config.fp8 is not None / self.fp4_enabled = config.fp4 is not None unconditionally. The mamba-stack attention linears, however, are kept in bf16 to preserve numerics. Capturing those layers with FP8 enabled wrapped their GEMMs in FP8 cast paths, silently quantizing weights that were intentionally meant to stay in bf16.
records.invariant: If isinstance(base_module, TransformerLayer) and config.keep_mamba_stack_attention_linear_in_bf16 and not is_moe_layer, runner.fp8_enabled and runner.fp4_enabled must both be False.

records.title: TransformerLayer with moe_layer_recompute uses non-FP4-aware te_checkpoint guard, so FP4 recompute uses tensor_parallel.checkpoint and loses FP4 amax tracking
records.root_cause: TransformerLayer.forward selected te_checkpoint only when self.config.fp8. With FP4-only training, the gate was False, so the regular tensor_parallel.checkpoint was used. That recompute path does not know about TE's FP recipe machinery: amax history is not extended for the recomputed forward, so the next forward sees an amax that omits the contribution of the recomputed pass, yielding mismatched scales between forward and recompute.
records.invariant: When self.is_moe_layer and self.moe_layer_recompute and (config.fp8 or config.fp4), te_checkpoint must be selected as the recompute function.

records.title: group_limited_topk uses num_groups instead of topk in inner topk
Attention.set_save_original_input gate is FP8-only and missed for NVFP4, so attention activations are cached as the FP4-quantized tensor instead of the original input
records.root_cause: Attention.__init__ guarded set_save_original_input on the linear_proj only when config.fp8 and recipe != delayed. With FP4 training, the guard never fired so linear_proj kept the FP4-quantized tensor cache. When selective recompute later invoked the saved tensor for backward, it operated on the quantized tensor instead of the bf16 original input, producing a recompute that mismatches the forward.
records.invariant: set_save_original_input must be called on TELinear modules whenever (config.fp8 with non-delayed recipe and TE>=2.6.0dev0) OR (config.fp4 and TE>=2.7.0.dev0).

records.title: MultimodalRotaryEmbedding slices rotary embedding along the wrong dimension and omits cp_group when CP is enabled, so each CP rank sees the wrong rotary position embedding
records.root_cause: After emb.transpose(0, 1).contiguous() the sequence dimension is index 0, but get_pos_emb_on_this_cp_rank was called with seq_dim=1 and no cp_group argument. The wrong axis was sharded across CP ranks, and the default global cp_group fallback was used instead of the configured one. Each CP rank ended up with a rotary slice that does not correspond to its own sequence partition.
records.invariant: MultimodalRotaryEmbedding output for CP rank r must equal get_pos_emb_on_this_cp_rank(global_emb, seq_dim=0, group=cp_group) for the configured cp_group.

records.title: MambaStack assigns make_viewless_tensor result to local 'output' but returns 'hidden_states', sending a non-viewless aliased tensor between hybrid VPP stages
records.root_cause: MambaStack.forward stored the result of make_viewless_tensor in a local variable 'output', but the function ultimately returned hidden_states. So the explicit make_viewless_tensor call had no effect. The non-viewless tensor (still a view onto an internal buffer) was returned and forwarded to the next PP stage via isend; on a hybrid VPP schedule the underlying buffer was reused before isend completed, and the next stage received corrupted activations.
records.invariant: MambaStack.forward must return a tensor that is viewless (.is_view() == False) so its storage is not aliased with internal stack buffers.

records.title: Hybrid DSL CommonLayerConfig does not derive params_dtype from mixed_precision_dtype, so models with mixed_precision_dtype='bf16' silently keep params_dtype=fp32
records.root_cause: The DSL allowed bf16 mixed-precision compute while keeping params_dtype at fp32, producing a TransformerConfig with bf16=True but params_dtype=torch.float32. The legacy --bf16 CLI path automatically aligns params_dtype with bf16, so the DSL path silently diverged: parameters were materialized in fp32 and then cast on every forward, doubling memory and changing numerics relative to the legacy path.
records.invariant: When TransformerConfig.bf16 is True (mixed_precision_dtype='bf16') and the recipe leaves params_dtype at the fp32 default, the produced TransformerConfig.params_dtype must equal torch.bfloat16.

records.title: ChainedOptimizer.split_state_dict for single-chunk MoE only assigns to state_dicts[0], leaving all other sub-optimizers unaware of the model state and silently skipping their load
records.root_cause: split_state_dict's single-model-chunk branch did state_dicts[0] = state_dict only, leaving state_dicts[1:] as None. Sub-optimizers beyond index 0 (e.g. the MoE expert optimizer) thus received None as their model state and silently skipped loading their parameters/optimizer states. The model proceeded with default-initialized expert parameters after a checkpoint resume.
records.invariant: After ChainedOptimizer.split_state_dict, every entry in state_dicts must be non-None when state_dict is provided and len(self.model_chunks) == 1.

records.title: MegatronOptimizer.get_grads_for_norm checks fsdp_param BEFORE precision-aware-optimizer branch, so M-FSDP + precision-aware optimizer reads param.grad._local_tensor instead of decoupled_grad and computes the wrong norm
records.root_cause: MegatronOptimizer.get_grads_for_norm gated on getattr(param, '__fsdp_param__', False) FIRST and only fell back to the precision-aware decoupled_grad branch when not an FSDP param. With both flags on, FSDP parameters were always read via param.grad._local_tensor instead of param.decoupled_grad. Under precision-aware optimizer, param.grad is None or stale because gradients are written into param.decoupled_grad. The grad norm computation thus used wrong (likely zero) tensors, silently disabling clipping and giving an incorrect global norm for logging.
records.invariant: When config.use_precision_aware_optimizer_no_fp8_or_ds_fp8 is True, get_grads_for_norm must use param.decoupled_grad (with ._local_tensor when also __fsdp_param__) and never use param.grad.

records.title: Hybrid MoE pad_granularity is set to 32 (MXFP8) instead of 128 (HybridEP), so per-CP-rank sequence shards are misaligned for HybridEP dispatcher
records.root_cause: HybridCPDataLoaderWrapper used pad_granularity = 32 (MXFP8 block size) when computing per-rank padding. HybridEP requires alignment to 128 elements. With granularity 32, per-CP-rank shards landed at offsets that did not satisfy HybridEP's 128-element alignment, so the dispatcher's load/store kernels read/wrote across token boundaries, mixing tokens between adjacent ranks.
records.invariant: HybridCPDataLoaderWrapper.pad_granularity must equal 128 when HybridEP is enabled (instead of 32).

records.title: MegatronOptimizer uses use_precision_aware_optimizer instead of use_precision_aware_optimizer_no_fp8_or_ds_fp8 when selecting decoupled_grad, so FP8 + precision-aware paths read param.decoupled_grad which is None and report grad_norm=0
records.root_cause: MegatronOptimizer.get_grads_for_norm and clip_grad_by_total_norm_fp32 dispatched on self.config.use_precision_aware_optimizer. With FP8 enabled, decoupled_grad is intentionally NOT used for those parameters; they should fall back to param.grad. The buggy gate took the precision-aware path anyway, attempting to read param.decoupled_grad (which is None), so grads_for_norm came back empty and grad_norm computed to 0.0. Without proper gradient clipping the optimizer could overshoot, but no exception was raised because count_zeros and clip routines treat empty input as a valid no-op.
records.invariant: When config.fp8 is set or config.fp8_recipe in the DS_FP8 family, get_grads_for_norm must follow the param.grad branch (not param.decoupled_grad).

records.title: z-loss metric tracking missing avg_group — not averaged across ranks
config.softmax_scale ignored in attention forward paths
Attention norm modifies the residual stream
records.root_cause: x = self.attn_norm(x) overwrites the residual variable. Residual connection uses normed input instead of original input.
records.invariant: After attn_norm, the residual tensor must be the original input, not the normed version

records.title: Z-loss calculation averaged over instances instead of tokens
records.root_cause: z_loss / num_micro_batches instead of z_loss / batch_size_in_tokens (64x difference for seq_len=64)
records.invariant: z_loss denominator must be batch_size_in_tokens, not num_micro_batches

records.title: preserve_rng_state incorrectly set to False with dropout
records.root_cause: Boolean condition inverted: preserve_rng_state = (all_dropout==0) instead of not(all_dropout==0)
records.invariant: When dropout > 0, preserve_rng_state must be True

records.title: start_index not reset in data loader
records.root_cause: global_step not reset to 0 when restore_dataloader=False
records.invariant: When restore_dataloader=False, global_step must be reset to 0

records.title: Wrong size calculation for QK layer norm with GQA
records.invariant: k_norm size must equal head_dim * n_kv_heads, not d_model // n_kv_heads

records.title: SkipStepAdamW step state never incremented
records.root_cause: optimizer step counter stays at 0, biasing Adam bias correction
records.invariant: After N optimizer.step() calls, state['step'] must equal N

records.title: Non-zero ranks reporting partially-reduced metrics
records.root_cause: Throughput metrics not using reduce_type=max → partially-reduced values on non-zero ranks
records.invariant: Throughput metrics must use reduce_type=ReduceType.max

records.title: Initial LR not set in optimizer param_groups
records.root_cause: Missing initial_lr in param_groups breaks LR scheduler after checkpoint resume
records.invariant: After optimizer construction, all param_groups must contain initial_lr

records.title: Mixture rounding error causing sample repetition
records.root_cause: Missing global_batch_size in SourceMixtureDatasetConfig causes rounding error
records.invariant: Config must include global_batch_size for proper allocation

records.title: SourceMixtureDatasetConfig overrides global random seed
records.root_cause: build() calls random.seed(self.seed), corrupting global RNG state
records.invariant: build() must not call global random.seed()

records.title: Incorrect label_mask tensor creation in NumpyPaddedFSLDataset
records.root_cause: torch.ones_like(input_ids) creates int64 mask, padded with pad_token_id instead of bool+False
records.invariant: label_mask must be bool dtype with False padding

records.title: Integer overflow when tracking global flops
records.root_cause: global_train_flops: int overflows after ~107K steps for 7B models
records.invariant: global flops tracking must use float to avoid overflow

records.title: A100 peak flops specification 2x too low
records.root_cause: A100 BF16 peak = 624 TFLOPS but code used 312 TFLOPS, inflating MFU to unrealistic values.
records.invariant: A100 BF16 peak flops must be 624 TFLOPS, not 312

records.title: RMSNorm uses L2 norm instead of root-mean-square — wrong normalization
records.root_cause: x.norm(2) is L2 norm (sqrt(sum(x^2))), not RMS (sqrt(mean(x^2)))
records.invariant: After RMSNorm, output.pow(2).mean(-1) should be approximately 1.0

records.title: grad_norm_exp_avg EMA self-referential update — adaptive clipping broken
SDP attention bias not cast to autocast dtype, -inf downcasts to NaNs in mixed precision
records.root_cause: The attention bias was created in fp32 with -inf masked positions and only cast to the input dtype at the SDP call. Under autocast, the SDP kernel runs in lower precision; downcasting -inf to bf16/fp16 yields valid -inf values that propagate through softmax and produce NaNs once tokens are masked. The fix uses torch.finfo(target_dtype).min and casts the bias before the SDP call.
records.invariant: attention output must not contain NaNs after softmax when an attention mask is provided

records.title: FLOPs counter multiplies per-sequence flops by global batch size every step instead of accumulating per token
records.root_cause: num_fwd_flops/num_bck_flops were computed per sequence (multiplied by max_sequence_length) and SpeedMonitor accumulated them with global_batch_size every step using +=. After resume, the running total was overwritten/reset per step rather than treated as cumulative tokens, so reported Gflops did not accumulate across resumes. Fix changes flops to per-token and assigns Gflops = (fwd+bck) * global_total_tokens / 1e9.
records.invariant: total_training_Gflops must be a strictly non-decreasing function of global_total_tokens across training resumes

records.title: clip_grads_and_collect_metrics reduces grad norm over the global PG instead of the HSDP shard PG
records.root_cause: When training with HSDP each replica holds a full copy of the gradients, so reducing per-shard gradient norms over the WORLD process group double-counts grads across replicas. The original code called dist.reduce/dist.all_reduce without specifying a process group, so they used WORLD instead of the shard group. The fix accepts an optional process_group argument and routes every reduce/all_reduce call through it.
records.invariant: after reducing gradient norm metrics, the per-replica total_grad_norm should equal the un-replicated full-model norm; with N replicas, using the WORLD group would multiply the value by N

records.title: Outlier-loss skip-step logic inverted: optimizer steps only when loss IS an outlier
records.root_cause: should_step was being AND-ed with is_outlier, meaning the optimizer only stepped on outlier steps and silently skipped normal training steps. The fix negates is_outlier so the optimizer steps on normal batches and skips outliers as intended.
records.invariant: optim.step() must be invoked on the vast majority of training steps; should_step should equal True on non-outlier batches

records.title: torch.device('mps') used as boolean check is always truthy, forces every run into MPS/CPU mode
records.root_cause: The condition `if torch.device('mps')` is always True because torch.device(...) returns a non-None Device object. As a result the script unconditionally rewrites init_device to 'mps' and disables distributed training even on CUDA hosts. Fix replaces the call with torch.backends.mps.is_available() and a corresponding CPU check.
records.invariant: after script bootstrap, cfg.distributed_strategy and cfg.model.init_device must reflect the actual available backend (CUDA when torch.cuda.is_available())

records.title: muP set_base_shapes rescales parameters again when loading from a checkpoint, doubling the muP scaling
records.root_cause: OLMo.__init__ unconditionally invoked set_base_shapes(self, mup_base_shapes) which applies muP rescaling to the parameters. When loading a checkpoint, parameters are already in muP-scaled space, so the rescale fires a second time and silently shrinks/grows weights by the muP factor. Fix adds a mup_rescale_params=False kwarg and passes it from from_checkpoint.
records.invariant: for muP runs, parameter norms after OLMo.from_checkpoint() must equal the parameter norms saved in the checkpoint

records.title: Restart LR/weight-decay reset uses cfg.learning_rate for every param group, ignoring per-group muP scaling
records.root_cause: On restart Trainer.restore_checkpoint reset every group's lr/initial_lr/weight_decay to cfg.optimizer.learning_rate / cfg.optimizer.weight_decay. With muP, matrix-like groups have lr divided by width_mult, so this reset wiped out muP scaling and used the base LR for every group. The fix tags each muP group with mup_lr/mup_weight_decay and uses those when resetting.
records.invariant: after restart, group['lr'] for a muP matrix-like group equals cfg.lr / width_mult, not cfg.lr

records.title: OLMoBlock 'normal' init divides ff_out by sqrt(2*n_layers), shrinking it 1/sqrt(2L) below the configured init_std
records.root_cause: In the 'normal' init branch ff_out.weight was further divided by sqrt(2 * n_layers) after init_normal, supposedly to compensate for it being a residual layer. This left the per-row std much smaller than the configured init_std and broke equivalence with the full_megatron path. Fix removes the post-init divisor and unifies the std/cutoff_factor selection across init_fn variants.
records.invariant: for init_fn=normal the std of OLMoBlock.ff_out.weight at initialization should equal config.init_std (within sampling noise), not config.init_std / sqrt(2*n_layers)

records.title: Attention causal mask inverted — future tokens attend to past
records.root_cause: 1 - triu() masks the lower triangle instead of upper, inverting causal attention
records.invariant: In causal attention, position 0 should only attend to itself (avg attended index = 0)

records.title: ff_out readout reset overwrites muP zero-init weights with normal-distribution values
records.root_cause: OLMo.reset_parameters always called init_normal on transformer.ff_out, including under muP where ff_out is a MuReadout that must be initialized to zero. The non-zero initialization breaks the muP coordinate-check property and changes the model's effective output scale at initialization. Fix skips init_normal on ff_out when use_mup is True.
records.invariant: for use_mup=true, transformer.ff_out.weight must be all zeros immediately after model construction

records.title: OLMoSequentialBlock.ff_proj is silently zero-initialized via MuReadout when use_mup is enabled
records.root_cause: When use_mup was true, ff_proj was constructed as MuReadout with readout_zero_init=True and reset_parameters skipped re-initializing it. Only the final output ff_out should be a MuReadout in muP; every block's ff_proj being zero-initialized wipes out the FFN contribution at start of training. Fix only uses MuReadout for ff_proj when mlp_hidden_size is also set and always re-initializes ff_proj via init_normal.
records.invariant: for use_mup=true (and default mlp_hidden_size), each block's ff_proj.weight must have non-zero std after initialization

records.title: muP attention scale uses 1/d instead of sqrt(base_d)/d, mismatching the SP scale at the base width
records.root_cause: Under muP the attention scale was 1/q.size(-1), which differs from the standard parameterization scale 1/sqrt(d) even at the base width. This silently changes the attention temperature for the base model relative to SP. Fix uses sqrt(mup_base_n_heads)/q.size(-1) so that the scale matches SP exactly when n_heads == mup_base_n_heads and tracks muP scaling rules for wider models.
records.invariant: when use_mup=true and n_heads==mup_base_n_heads, attn_scale must equal 1/sqrt(head_dim) (the SP scale)

records.title: norm_after path applies attn_norm to (att_proj output) instead of to the attention output, leaving residual unnormed
records.root_cause: Under norm_after, attn_norm was being applied to the QKV projection output (qkv = attn_norm(att_proj(x))) before splitting and computing attention. The Post-LN attention design requires applying attn_norm to the attention output before the residual add. This silently changes the model semantics from Post-LN attention to a normalized-QKV attention.
records.invariant: for norm_after=true, the tensor flowing into att_proj must be unnormed; attn_norm must be applied to the attention output (att) prior to the residual add

records.title: global_step not reset when restore_dataloader=False, so resumed runs keep the checkpoint's step counter
records.root_cause: When the user sets restore_dataloader=False to start from saved weights but a fresh dataset, restore_checkpoint() resets epoch and token counters but forgot to reset global_step. The optimizer/LR scheduler then starts at the checkpoint's step (e.g., 50000) instead of 0, silently skipping warmup and using a much smaller LR than expected.
records.invariant: when cfg.restore_dataloader is False after restore_checkpoint(), self.global_step must equal 0

records.title: Multi-epoch training does not reset dataset.start_index, so the next epoch resumes from the previous epoch's offset
records.root_cause: On epoch rollover Trainer reset epoch counters and called dataset.reshuffle(), but never reset dataset.start_index. The IterableDataset therefore skipped the first global_train_examples_seen_this_epoch instances of the new epoch, silently dropping them from training.
records.invariant: at the start of every epoch, self.dataset.start_index must equal 0

records.title: Restart in later epochs uses seed+epoch as PRNG seed, mixing epoch into seed irreversibly and corrupting reshuffle
records.root_cause: IterableDataset was constructed with seed=seed+(train_config.epoch or 0) and reshuffle() did self.seed += 1. After a restart at epoch=N the dataset received seed+N as base and then was incremented again, producing a different shuffle order than the original run had used at the same epoch. This silently changed the data ordering across resumes.
records.invariant: the global indices produced by IterableDataset for (seed, epoch) must be identical across a fresh run and a resumed run

records.title: Optimizer metric tensors are kept on CPU, causing per-rank cross-device mismatch on the all_reduce path
records.root_cause: per_param_min/max/sum/norm tensors were appended without explicit device, defaulting to CPU. The subsequent dist.all_reduce was then performed on CPU tensors while NCCL only supports GPU tensors; this either silently used the gloo backend (different reduction semantics, slower) or returned partially-reduced values when ranks ended up on different devices. Fix forces all metric tensors to the GPU device.
records.invariant: every tensor passed to dist.all_reduce/dist.reduce in clip_grads_and_collect_metrics must reside on the CUDA device, not CPU

records.title: z_loss mean reduction divides by mask fraction instead of masked mean
records.root_cause: z_squared / mask.mean() instead of (z_squared * mask).mean() — wrong reduction
records.invariant: z_loss with mean reduction should be a scalar; buggy version returns unreduced tensor

records.title: MoE load-balance and z-loss aux losses logged without all-reduce, so each rank reports its local value
records.root_cause: In Trainer the cross-entropy and z-loss were reduced across all ranks before logging, but lb_batch_loss (MoE load-balancing loss) and moe_z_batch_loss were missed. Each rank logged its local value, so the wandb metric reflected only rank 0's mini-batch instead of the global mean, giving misleading load-balance behavior and misreporting MoE training health.
records.invariant: after the metric reduction block, lb_batch_loss and moe_z_batch_loss must be identical on every rank (mean across ranks)

records.title: Optimizer collects metrics with num_model_replicas == 1 hardcoded, so HSDP norms are N times too large
records.root_cause: Optimizer.clip_grads_and_collect_metrics divided by a hardcoded num_model_replicas=1 even when HSDP was using multiple replicas. Each replica contributed identical gradient norms; without dividing by the replica count, all_reduce sums them and the reported norm is N times the true value, leading to spurious clipping decisions and wrong logged grad_norm.
records.invariant: with N model replicas in HSDP, all_reduced grad_norm metric must be divided by N before being reported

records.title: Reduced sums/norms not divided by num_model_replicas in HSDP, optimizer metrics inflated by replica count
records.root_cause: After the dist.all_reduce(SUM) in HYBRID_SHARD, identical replica contributions are summed N times. The original code consumed those sums directly, so per-param avg metrics and grad_norm metrics ended up N times larger than the true value. Fix divides the all-reduced tensor (all_sums_norms_numels and all_norms) by self.num_model_replicas before splitting and using.
records.invariant: for HSDP with N replicas, sum_after_all_reduce / N must equal the true global sum; per_param_avg_metrics computed from this should match a reference single-replica run

records.title: FullCheckpointer rebuilds optim state with old parameter keys, dropping state for renamed params after block_group_size change
records.root_cause: _make_state_dict_compatible returned a remapped state_dict but FullCheckpointer threw away the og_keys_to_new mapping when calling load_fsdp_optim_state. The optimizer state was then loaded against the new model keys without translation, so optimizer state for many params was either silently zeroed or attached to the wrong tensor.
records.invariant: after FullCheckpointer.restore_checkpoint with load_optimizer_state=True, optimizer.state must contain entries for every parameter in fsdp_model.parameters() and the values must match the saved checkpoint

records.title: param-group classifier uses '.norm.' regex requiring trailing dot, treating q_norm/k_norm/ff_norm leaf weights as decay params
records.root_cause: get_param_groups identified norm parameters via the substring '.norm.' which only matches when there is a child name after .norm. For QK layer norms (q_norm.weight, k_norm.weight) the FQN ends with '.q_norm.weight' so the dot after norm never appears and the weight is silently routed to the decay group, applying weight_decay to a normalization layer's gain.
records.invariant: all parameters whose name contains '.norm' (with or without a child) must end up in the no_decay group when no_decay_norm_and_bias is true

records.title: all_sums_norms_numels concatenated along last dim and reduced wrongly, mixing sums/norms/numels into one slot
records.root_cause: all_sums.unsqueeze(-1), all_norms.unsqueeze(-1), all_numels.unsqueeze(-1) were concatenated on dim=-1 and then reduced. After dist.reduce, all_sums_norms_numels.split(1) split per-parameter rows instead of separating the three categories, so the per-param avg metrics became a meaningless mix of sums/norms/numels.
records.invariant: after dist.reduce and split(1), the three pieces all_sums/all_norms/all_numels must each have shape (num_params,)

records.title: DataConfig defaults memmap_dtype to uint16 silently, so vocab_size > 2^16 truncates token ids on load
records.root_cause: Before this commit MemMapDataset was constructed without passing a memmap_dtype, defaulting to uint16. When the actual on-disk file was uint32 (because vocab_size > 2^16), reading two-byte chunks silently produced wrong token ids without any type error. Fix exposes effective_memmap_dtype on DataConfig and threads it through build_memmap_dataset.
records.invariant: MemMapDataset(memmap_dtype) must equal np.uint32 (or wider) when train_config.model.vocab_size > 2**16

records.title: _do_adaptive_clipping/_do_global_fixed_clipping hardcode collect_param_metrics=True, forcing per-step host-device sync and ignoring metrics_log_interval
records.root_cause: The clipping helpers were called with collect_param_metrics=True every step, regardless of the outer collect_param_metrics flag. This silently bypassed the metrics_log_interval gate (forcing host-device sync to compute clipping_rate every step) and produced metric values that did not match the requested logging cadence.
records.invariant: when collect_param_metrics is False at the outer call, _do_adaptive_clipping/_do_global_fixed_clipping must also be invoked with collect_param_metrics=False and clipping_rate must not be added to all_metrics

records.title: RoPE sin/cos missing type_as — dtype mismatch in mixed precision
records.root_cause: pos_sin/pos_cos cached in float32, not cast to match q_ dtype (bf16/fp16)
records.invariant: In apply_rotary_pos_emb, pos_sin.dtype and pos_cos.dtype must match t.dtype

records.title: Mitchell init hardcodes cutoff_factor=3.0, ignoring user-supplied init_cutoff_factor across blocks and embeddings
records.root_cause: Every Mitchell-init code path (OLMoBlock, OLMoSequentialBlock, OLMoLlamaBlock, and OLMo wte init) literally assigned cutoff_factor = 3.0, completely ignoring config.init_cutoff_factor. User configs that set a different cutoff (e.g. 4 or 6) silently produced narrower truncated-normal weight distributions than requested.
records.invariant: for init_fn=mitchell, the cutoff_factor used by init_normal must equal config.init_cutoff_factor (falling back to 3.0 only when None)

records.title: Final linear-decay scheduler uses wrong start/end factors (decays from 1.0 to alpha_f instead of alpha_f to alpha_f^2)
records.root_cause: The final linear decay segment is meant to take over after a cosine schedule has already decayed the LR to alpha_f * base_lr. The buggy version constructed `LinearLR(start_factor=1.0, end_factor=alpha_f)` which jumps the LR back up to the base learning rate at the handoff, and then decays only to alpha_f over the tail. The correct settings continue from `alpha_f` down to `alpha_f**2`. Result is a silent LR spike + wrong final LR.
records.invariant: scheduler.get_last_lr() must be continuous across the cosine-to-linear handoff at step=t_max

records.title: Embedding init std missing sqrt(d_model) factor — embeddings 16x too small
records.root_cause: init_std used directly instead of init_std * sqrt(d_model) for embeddings
records.invariant: embedding weight std should be init_std * sqrt(d_model)

records.title: IterableDataset leftover indices distributed wrongly across workers
records.root_cause: When distributing the leftover (unaligned) indices across workers, the buggy code did `left_overs = indices[truncated_size + worker_info.id : truncated_size + worker_info.id + worker_info.num_workers]`, which gives each worker a contiguous slice of `num_workers` indices starting at its id (so workers overlap and miss other leftovers). The fix uses strided slicing `indices[truncated_size + worker_info.id :: worker_info.num_workers]` so each worker independently picks its share.
records.invariant: Union of leftover indices across all workers must equal the full set of leftover indices, with no overlap

records.title: Dataset start_index not reset when starting a new epoch
records.root_cause: On epoch rollover the trainer set `self.epoch = epoch + 1` and reset `global_train_examples_seen_this_epoch = 0`, called `dataset.reshuffle()`, but forgot to reset `self.dataset.start_index = 0`. The IterableDataset therefore continued slicing the new (reshuffled) global indices starting from the previous epoch's offset, dropping that prefix of the new epoch and shortening it by the same amount.
records.invariant: At the start of every epoch the dataset must yield exactly len(dataset) examples in that epoch

records.title: Block readout init unconditionally re-initializes ff_proj, overwriting muP zero-init
records.root_cause: OLMoSequentialBlock.reset_parameters unconditionally called `init_normal(self.ff_proj, std, cutoff_factor, ...)`. When `use_mup=True`, ff_proj is a `MuReadout` module whose readout weights must remain at the muP zero/special initialization; the unconditional re-init overwrites that with a regular truncated-normal, silently breaking the muP coordinate-check guarantee that activation magnitudes are width-independent.
records.invariant: If use_mup=True, ff_proj.weight at end of init must remain at MuReadout's zero/scaled init (not truncated-normal with std=init_std)

records.title: q_norm forced to elementwise_affine=True regardless of attention_layer_norm_with_affine
records.root_cause: When constructing QK normalization layers, `k_norm` correctly used `elementwise_affine=config.attention_layer_norm_with_affine` but `q_norm` was hard-coded to `elementwise_affine=True`. With `attention_layer_norm_with_affine=False` the model silently normalizes q with learnable scale/bias but k without, breaking symmetry between q and k and adding parameters that the user did not request.
records.invariant: q_norm.weight.requires_grad == k_norm.weight.requires_grad; both must follow attention_layer_norm_with_affine

records.title: Token embedding sized by vocab_size instead of embedding_size, mismatching ff_out width
records.root_cause: wte was constructed with `nn.Embedding(config.vocab_size, ...)` but the output projection `ff_out` was sized for `config.embedding_size or config.vocab_size`. When embedding_size > vocab_size, ff_out has more output classes than the embedding table has rows, so the extra logits backprop into nothing on the embedding side and the loss is computed over rows that have no corresponding learnable embedding. Logits for ids in [vocab_size, embedding_size) silently bias the softmax denominator.
records.invariant: wte.num_embeddings must equal ff_out.out_features (= embedding_size or vocab_size)

records.title: Flash attention input layout wrong — head and sequence dims swapped
records.root_cause: flash_attn expects (B,S,H,D) but receives (B,H,S,D) without transpose
records.invariant: flash_attn input dim1 must be seq_len, not num_heads

records.title: Missing reset_parameters() after FSDP wrap on torch>=2.1 leaves model with default-initialized weights
records.root_cause: Starting in torch 2.1, FSDP no longer triggers the user's reset_parameters() automatically when materializing meta-device parameters. The buggy script created the OLMo model with init_device='meta', wrapped with FSDP, and never explicitly called `olmo_model.reset_parameters()` afterwards. Parameters are therefore left with whatever default contents FSDP produces (effectively uninitialized/zero-filled), silently destroying the carefully designed init scheme.
records.invariant: After FSDP wrap, summary stats of every parameter must match the init_fn's expected mean/std

records.title: ff_out nn.Linear constructed without device=init_device, breaking meta-init flow
records.root_cause: When building the readout `ff_out`, every other Linear in the model passed `device=config.init_device` so it could be created on the meta device and later materialized by FSDP with the configured init. The buggy version omitted this kwarg for `ff_out`, so it was always built on the default device with default kaiming init, escaping the init pipeline. The readout therefore carries the wrong init scale and lives on the wrong device until FSDP later moves it.
records.invariant: After model construction, every learnable parameter's device must equal config.init_device

records.title: load_model in mup coord-check skips reset_parameters when infshapes is None
records.root_cause: `reset_parameters()` was nested inside `if infshapes is not None:` together with `apply_infshapes`. For the standard-parametrization baseline (`infshapes=None`) the code therefore skipped reset_parameters entirely, leaving FSDP-materialized parameters with their default (often near-zero) values. Comparison curves and any downstream training look completely off without raising an error.
records.invariant: olmo_model.reset_parameters() must be called whenever the model is freshly built, regardless of mup mode

records.title: DeepSpeed scheduler set to WarmupLR instead of WarmupDecayLR (no decay phase)
records.root_cause: DeepSpeedTrainer built its DeepSpeed config with `"scheduler": {"type": "WarmupLR", ...}`. WarmupLR only ramps up to the max LR and then holds it constant—it never decays. The intended schedule was WarmupDecayLR which ramps then linearly decays. Buggy training therefore runs at peak LR for the entire post-warmup duration, silently overshooting the planned schedule.
records.invariant: After warmup, learning rate must be monotonically decreasing toward warmup_min_lr; not constant

records.title: DeepSpeed warmup_min_lr=0 instead of base_lr*0.1, also missing warmup_type=linear
records.root_cause: DeepSpeedTrainer hard-coded `warmup_min_lr=0.0` and omitted `warmup_type='linear'`. Combined, the warmup ramp starts from exactly 0 (rather than 10% of base lr) and uses DeepSpeed's default warmup interpolation, producing a different shape than the OLMo trainer for the equivalent config. Training runs to completion but with a silently mismatched warmup schedule.
records.invariant: DeepSpeed warmup LR profile must match the OLMo trainer's warmup profile for an equivalent configuration

records.title: Newest checkpoint deleted by retention policy because it is appended after pruning
records.root_cause: Both `save_checkpoint` and `save_unsharded_checkpoint` appended the freshly-saved directory to `self.checkpoints`/`self.unsharded_checkpoints` *after* the deletion loop. The deletion loop ran on the old list (without the new entry), then the new entry was appended—but on the *next* save the just-saved checkpoint was already at the end and could be evicted in the wrong order. The fix appends before the dist.barrier so retention always sees the new entry.
records.invariant: After save_checkpoint(N), the directory step{N} must remain on disk and self.checkpoints must reflect the actual contents of save_folder

records.title: Train DataLoader max_steps not multiplied by device_train_batch_size
records.root_cause: `build_train_dataloader` passed `max_steps=train_config.max_duration` to the IterableDataset, but max_steps for the dataset is measured in *examples*, not optimizer steps. With device_train_batch_size > 1 the dataset truncates itself to max_duration examples instead of max_duration*batch_size examples, so the loader exhausts after roughly 1/batch_size of the planned training. Likewise `start_step` was not scaled, so resume-from-step doesn't seek to the right example.
records.invariant: Total examples yielded by train loader = max_duration * device_train_batch_size

records.title: Ladder 150M model uses max_sequence_length=1024 instead of 2048
records.root_cause: MODEL_CONFIG_150M in scripts/ladder.py hard-coded `max_sequence_length=1024`, half the standard ladder context length of 2048. The model is built with positional structures (rope cache, default attention bias buffers) sized for 1024 and the loader truncates training sequences to 1024 tokens, silently wasting the second half of every example and producing per-token loss numbers that are not comparable to the rest of the ladder.
records.invariant: Each tier in the ladder must use the same max_sequence_length (2048) so token-loss curves are comparable

records.title: Fused cross_entropy path passes lse_square_scale=0 so z-loss term is silently dropped
records.root_cause: In `fused_loss_fn` the call to FlashAttention's CrossEntropyLoss hard-coded `lse_square_scale=0.0`. That parameter is the multiplier for the auxiliary z-loss term that the fused kernel computes; setting it to 0 silently disables the z-loss in the fused path, even though the surrounding code believes z-loss is being applied (and adds it to the total loss with whatever value the kernel returned). With fused_loss enabled, training therefore runs without the intended z-regularization despite logging non-zero z_loss values.
records.invariant: z_loss returned by fused_loss_fn must have the same magnitude as z_loss returned by the python reference cross_entropy_loss for the same inputs

records.title: Ladder script uses eos_token_id=0 instead of dolma tokenizer's 50279
records.root_cause: `MODEL_CONFIG_150M` hard-coded `eos_token_id=0` even though the dolma GPT-NeoX tokenizer uses 50279 for end-of-document. With the wrong eos_token_id the model treats id 0 (an ordinary BPE token) as document boundary for chunk boundaries / loss masking, and never recognizes the real EOS appended by the tokenizer. Document boundary statistics and EOS-conditioned generation are silently wrong.
records.invariant: model.eos_token_id must equal tokenizer.eos_token_id (50279 for dolma GPT-NeoX)

records.title: Wrong layer initialized — ff_out instead of ff_proj (variable name typo)
MoE load-balancing loss not divided by num_micro_batches in gradient accumulation loop
records.root_cause: Inside the per-micro-batch loop the buggy code added the full `batched_load_balancing_loss(self.moe_args)` to the per-micro-batch loss without dividing by `len(micro_batches)`. Because the auxiliary loss is computed per micro batch but enters the optimizer once per global batch via gradient accumulation, the LB regularizer is silently scaled by N (the number of micro batches), pushing the router much harder toward uniformity than configured.
records.invariant: Sum of LB-loss contributions over a global batch must equal `batched_load_balancing_loss` evaluated once on the global batch (independent of micro-batch count)

records.title: Attention norm overwrites residual input — destroys identity path
Token IDs silently truncated to 16-bit by modulo 2^16
soft_target_probs silently truncated from float to int by as_tensor()
records.root_cause: Local as_tensor() casts non-bool numpy arrays via astype(np.int_), destroying float probabilities
records.invariant: as_tensor(float_array) must preserve float dtype, not truncate to int

records.title: Qwen3 transformer config defaults rope_full_precision=True, diverging from HF that applies RoPE in bf16
records.root_cause: TransformerConfig.qwen3_* factories did not pass rope_full_precision=False, so olmo-core promoted q/k to fp32 around the rotary multiply while HuggingFace Qwen3 applies RoPE entirely in bf16. The fp32 round-off difference made post-RoPE q/k bit-non-identical and silently shifted training dynamics from the HF reference.
records.invariant: When matching HF Qwen3, the dtype of the tensor entering the rotary multiplication must equal the input attention dtype (bf16), not fp32.

records.title: Attention claude-init uses d_model**-0.5 instead of actual w.in_features**-0.5 — wrong std for GQA Q/K/V and w_out
records.root_cause: InitMethod.attention used a single std = d_model**-0.5 for Q/K/V and w_out. Under GQA the K/V projection input is still d_model but the constant assumed identical fan-in across all weights, and for w_out the actual fan-in is n_heads*head_dim which can differ from d_model. Initialization was therefore silently scaled wrong on these layers.
records.invariant: Init std for each linear layer w must equal w.in_features**-0.5 (true fan-in), not a single d_model-derived constant shared across all attention projections.

records.title: Per-document RoPE positions not propagated when cu_doc_lens is provided in packed mode
records.root_cause: Attention.forward called self.rope(...) without forwarding the cu_doc_lens argument, so the second document in a packed sequence got global positions [k_doc1_len, ...] instead of restarting at 0. Documents that should have produced identical outputs silently received different rotary phases.
records.invariant: For two identical documents packed back-to-back, the post-RoPE q/k for both segments must match (intra-doc positions reset at each cu_doc_lens boundary).

records.title: RotaryEmbedding cu_doc_lens path miscomputes positions for B>1 — second batch element reuses batch-0 doc layout
records.root_cause: The cu_doc_lens code path built positions = arange(k_len) without adding any per-batch offset, then ran searchsorted against the flat cumulative-doc-lens list. For B>1 the second batch element's positions were searched against batch-0 boundaries, producing wrong doc indices and wrong intra-doc positions whenever batch elements had different doc layouts.
records.invariant: Local positions computed for each (batch, token) must equal token_index minus the start of that token's document; batch elements with identical doc structure must give identical local_positions.

records.title: GatedDeltaNet A_log/dt_bias initialized as empty (uninit memory) and miss the GDN-prescribed init
records.root_cause: GatedDeltaNet's A_log was initialized via torch.log(uniform(0,16)) and dt_bias via inverse-softplus on uniform(dt_min, dt_max), but the surrounding generic InitMethod did not delegate to the mixer, so for hybrid models these parameters silently fell back to torch.empty (uninitialized memory) or default linear inits — producing wildly off-distribution updates with no error.
records.invariant: After init, GDN A_log lies in log(uniform(0,16)) and dt_bias is the inverse-softplus of dt sampled in [dt_min, dt_max]; their distribution must be checkable against this prescription.

records.title: MoE load-balancing aux loss accumulated to metrics twice when activation checkpointing recomputes the block
records.root_cause: compute_aux_loss accumulated the load-balancing scalar into the per-step metric on every forward call. Activation checkpointing reruns forward during backward, so the aux loss was added twice, producing wandb metrics that are 2x the true value (gradient is unaffected but anyone using the metric to tune the multiplier is misled).
records.invariant: Metric accumulation inside the MoE router must occur exactly once per global forward — recompute calls must skip the metrics side-effect.

records.title: Idealized-overlap ladder reads dolma2 (uint32) tokens with default uint16 dtype — silently produces garbage token ids
records.root_cause: PerFileChunkedInstanceSourceConfig defaulted token_dtype to uint16. dolma2 stores token IDs as uint32 because the vocab exceeds 65535. Reading the file as uint16 reinterprets each pair of bytes as a different token, so the model trained on totally fabricated token streams without any error.
records.invariant: Configured token_dtype must accommodate tokenizer.vocab_size (uint16 only when vocab <= 65535).

records.title: OLMo midtraining mix key references the wrong file — '0625' name maps to '0725' path
records.root_cause: The DataMix enum had OLMo_midtraining_mix_0625_100B = 'OLMo-midtraining-mix-0725-100B'. The mismatched value silently routed users to the July (0725) mix when they thought they were using the June (0625) mix, training on the wrong corpus.
records.invariant: DataMix enum string value must match its enum member name (date components agree).

records.title: QwenRMSNorm absent from olmo-core — RMSNorm casts back to og_dtype after weight multiply, diverging from HF Qwen3
records.root_cause: olmo-core's RMSNorm computed normalize -> weight-multiply -> cast(og_dtype), which performs the affine multiply in fp32. HF's Qwen3RMSNorm casts back to og_dtype before the weight multiply so the multiply happens in input bf16. Trained Qwen3 weights expect the bf16 ordering; computing the multiply in fp32 silently drifts on outlier-feature channels deep in the stack.
records.invariant: For Qwen3 layer norm the weight*x multiply executes in input dtype (bf16), not in fp32 — equivalently x is cast back to og_dtype before the affine.

records.title: Activation checkpointing skips RNG state preservation even when dropout is active — backward recomputes a different mask
records.root_cause: Transformer.apply_activation_checkpointing hard-coded preserve_rng_state=False with a TODO. With dropout active, the recomputed forward in backward used a fresh random mask, so backward gradients corresponded to a different forward graph than the one used to produce the loss — silently wrong gradients and degraded convergence.
records.invariant: If any nn.Dropout module exists, the forward run during backward recompute must use the same RNG state as the original forward (preserve_rng_state=True).

records.title: Adam step counter not incremented — bias correction permanently wrong
records.root_cause: step.add_(step_factor) was commented out in adamw_step
records.invariant: optimizer state step must increment each training step

records.title: Expert/router gradients zeroed unconditionally in train_batch — first-half mask applied even when freeze_experts is off
records.root_cause: The base TransformerTrainModule.train_batch unconditionally walked named_parameters and zeroed the first half of expert and router gradients. The freeze logic was supposed to only run for the FreezeTransformerTrainModule subclass, but its train_batch override had been moved to module level, so the parent ran the masking on every regular training run silently — half of every expert never got updated.
records.invariant: When freeze_experts is unset/'none', no expert or router parameter gradient may be force-zeroed by the train module.

records.title: Config encoding ignores field.init=False — non-init dataclass fields silently round-trip with stale values
records.root_cause: Config.as_dict iterated dataclasses.fields without filtering out fields whose init=False, so derived fields were dumped to the encoded dict and re-passed to the dataclass constructor on decode. Decode then either crashed on unknown kwargs or silently overwrote the post_init-derived value with a stale snapshot, breaking config round-trip equivalence.
records.invariant: Encoded Config dict must contain only fields whose .init is True; decoding then re-encoding must be a fixed point.

records.title: RoPE positions use global token index in packed mode — second document gets [k_doc1_len, ...] instead of [0, ...]
records.root_cause: RotaryEmbedding.forward computed positions = arange(k_len) and indexed pos_sin/pos_cos directly, ignoring document boundaries. Two identical documents at different positions inside the packed batch produced different post-RoPE q/k, breaking the intra-document independence assumption used by document-aware attention masking.
records.invariant: Two identical documents packed back-to-back must yield identical post-RoPE q/k values (per-document positions reset at each cu_doc_lens boundary).

records.title: PerFileChunkedInstanceSourceConfig defaults token_dtype to uint16 — silent token-id corruption for vocab > 65535
records.root_cause: PerFileChunkedInstanceSourceConfig.token_dtype defaulted to uint16. When the on-disk file is uint32 the loader silently reinterprets each pair of bytes as a separate token, producing wrong but in-range token IDs that never error.
records.invariant: token_dtype default must match the tokenizer's required width; if not specified, must be inferred from tokenizer.vocab_size or the constructor must error.

records.title: MoEFusedV2Optimizer reduces PP grad norm with _combine_norm (sum-of-norms) instead of _reduce_norm — over-counts gradient magnitude
records.root_cause: When reducing total_grad_norm across the PP group, the code called self._combine_norm (which adds rank-local norms instead of squaring/all-reducing/sqrt). This over-estimated the global gradient norm, which then drove gradient clipping to scale every step too aggressively without raising any error.
records.invariant: Global grad-norm reduction across PP must satisfy sqrt(sum(local_norm**2)), equivalent to the existing _reduce_norm helper, not naive summation of norm magnitudes.

records.title: SamplingInstanceSource cache write race — concurrent ladder runs overwrite each other's index files
records.root_cause: Local rank-0 always rewrote the indices file at startup. Concurrent jobs sharing the work directory raced via tmp_path.replace, leaving training reading partially-written or shuffled indices. Because the file name embeds the fingerprint, the contents are guaranteed identical, so silently using a stale half-written file (or rebuilding into the same name as another job) gave inconsistent ordering across runs.
records.invariant: If the deterministic-fingerprint indices file already exists, the rank must not rewrite it; cross-rank reads of the file must agree.

records.title: memmap_to_write tmp filename uses seeded random — concurrent writers collide on identical path under the same RNG seed
records.root_cause: memmap_to_write picked the temp filename via random.randint(0, 2**32) seeded by the global Python RNG. With identical seeds across ranks, each rank generated the same tmp_path; one rank's tmp_path.replace removed the file another rank was about to read, causing FileNotFoundError-style silent data shadowing or partial-content reads when a fallback masked the error.
records.invariant: Concurrent writers of the same file must use unique temp paths (entropy independent of the deterministic seed) and a missing tmp_path due to a concurrent rename must succeed if the destination exists.

records.title: MultiGroupDistributedDataParallel falls back to default group when dist is unavailable but never wires per-bucket grad reduce
records.root_cause: MoE-style parameters were reduced one-by-one through the existing DDP path, missing the view-based bucket optimization that batches grads of the same dtype/process_group into a single all-reduce. Under EP+DP MoE this both inflated NCCL volume and silently skipped the comm_dtype downcast on extra-large params, occasionally producing zero gradients for partial buckets.
records.invariant: Under MoE DDP each parameter's gradient must participate in exactly one all-reduce per step, with comm_dtype matching the configured bucket dtype.

records.title: Mamba.forward casts inputs using cached self.dtype — wrong dtype after FSDP wraps the conv1d weight
records.root_cause: Mamba.forward used self.dtype (snapshot at construction time) to cast x. After FSDP wrapped the inner conv1d, the actual parameter dtype changed but self.dtype was stale, so x flowed into the kernel in the wrong precision. The MambaSSM kernel still ran but produced silently wrong values.
records.invariant: Activation dtype entering Mamba.inner must equal the live conv1d weight dtype (recomputed per forward), not a constructor-time snapshot.

records.title: DTPBoundaryPredictor calls F.silu with two arguments — silu treats w3(h) as inplace flag, drops gating
records.root_cause: The expression F.silu(self.w1(h), self.w3(h)) passed self.w3(h) as the inplace argument of F.silu (PyTorch interprets the second positional as a bool-coerced inplace flag). The intended SwiGLU gate (silu(w1(h)) * w3(h)) never executed, so the FFN computed silu(w1(h)) alone and the boundary predictor produced silently degraded outputs.
records.invariant: FFN must implement gated SwiGLU: out = w2(silu(w1(h)) * w3(h)); silu must be called with exactly one tensor argument.

records.title: sqrt decay LR schedule uses wrong formula — decay curve inverted
records.root_cause: sqrt(progress) instead of 1-sqrt(1-progress) — wrong decay curve shape
records.invariant: sqrt decay should decay fast initially, slow at end

records.title: MoE sigmoid router gives F.sigmoid(logits) without epsilon — exact-zero scores propagate as NaN through downstream log
records.root_cause: scores = F.sigmoid(logits) could underflow to exactly 0.0 under low precision, and downstream load-balancing or aux-loss code took log/divide of the score, producing -inf/NaN that silently propagated into the final loss without any explicit error.
records.invariant: Router score for gating_function=sigmoid must be strictly positive (>= eps) so subsequent log/divide operations are finite.

records.title: fused_linear_cross_entropy_loss accumulates gradient in bf16 by default — silently noisier than fp32 accumulation
records.root_cause: The liger-kernel fused linear+CE call defaulted accum_grad to bf16, which silently degraded gradient precision on the LM head. The numerical noise was small enough that training continued, but it shifted loss curves vs the unfused baseline.
records.invariant: Backward gradient accumulation for the LM head fused kernel must be in fp32 even when forward inputs are bf16.

records.title: fan_in init for embeddings ignores embed_scale — embeddings remain std=1.0 and become huge after scaling
records.root_cause: init_embeddings under fan_in always used std=1.0. The transformer then multiplied embeddings by embed_scale (e.g., sqrt(d_model)) at the input, producing embeddings several orders of magnitude larger than intended. Training did not error but the input magnitude scrambled the early-layer dynamics.
records.invariant: After init_embeddings followed by the embed_scale multiply, the embedding output std must stay near 1.0 (compensating the fan-in init by 1/embed_scale).

records.title: NumpyDataLoaderBase double-counts tokens_processed — counter advances both inside and outside the iterator
records.root_cause: NumpyDataLoaderBase incremented self.tokens_processed += self.global_batch_size inside its __iter__ in addition to the trainer-level update, double-counting tokens. On resume the loader skipped twice as many batches as it should, silently advancing past unseen data.
records.invariant: tokens_processed must increase by exactly global_batch_size per yielded batch, not 2x.

records.title: ComplexRotaryEmbedding ignores cu_doc_lens — packed-document positions never reset for complex-RoPE blocks
records.root_cause: ComplexRotaryEmbedding.forward did not accept cu_doc_lens, so even when callers tried to enable per-document positions for complex-RoPE blocks, the call site silently fell through to global positions and the rotary phase still depended on global token index across packed boundaries.
records.invariant: Per-document positions used by complex-RoPE must reset at each cu_doc_lens boundary; identical packed documents must yield identical post-RoPE q/k.

records.title: Evaluator iterates with stale data-loader state — second eval pass starts mid-stream, evaluating a different subset
records.root_cause: Evaluator.__iter__ called reshuffle() but did not reset() the data loader. tokens_processed/batches_processed from the previous (truncated) eval persisted, so the next eval pass started reading from the stale offset instead of batch 0. Repeated evals on the same checkpoint silently scored on different data subsets.
records.invariant: Two consecutive Evaluator passes over the same checkpoint must read the same first-N batches when deterministic=True (epoch pinned).

records.title: Trainer async bookkeeping callback fires after future is FINISHED — state_dict snapshot can capture pre-callback state
records.root_cause: _run_bookkeeping_op attached cb via future.add_done_callback. add_done_callback runs after the future is marked FINISHED, so _join_bookkeeping_ops returned before cb ran, and a state_dict() capture immediately after could observe stale callback state (e.g., un-rotated checkpoint indexes).
records.invariant: All bookkeeping callbacks for a future must complete before that future transitions to FINISHED so _join_bookkeeping_ops waits on them too.

records.title: Grad clipper recorded grad_norm DTensor — record_metric saw distributed value
records.root_cause: GradClipperCallback recorded the raw grad_norm output from torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ without unwrapping it. With TP, this returned a DTensor; the metric system then operated on the DTensor across ranks, producing a wrongly reduced grad-norm value while clipping itself was already applied locally.
records.invariant: Values passed to record_metric with reduce_type=None must be plain tensors representing per-call values, never DTensors with implicit replication semantics.

records.title: PP grad-norm clip used per-PP-stage local norm without all-reducing across PP ranks
records.root_cause: TransformerTrainModule.optim_step took grad_norm from the per-stage clip path without summing the squared norms across PP ranks first. Each PP stage sees only its local parameters, so the unreduced norm is a fraction of the global norm; clipping uses too small a divisor, leaving gradients larger than max_grad_norm.
records.invariant: When PP is enabled, the gradient norm used for clip_grad_norm_ must be reduced across the PP mesh (sum-of-squares with sqrt) before applying max_norm.

records.title: NaN loss when all instances on a rank are masked — division by zero
records.root_cause: batch_num_tokens_for_loss = 0 when all instances masked, causing loss / 0 = NaN
records.invariant: batch_num_tokens_for_loss must be > 0 to avoid NaN in loss computation

records.title: Instance filter loss divisor missed masked-out instance tokens — wrong gradient scale
records.root_cause: When the instance filter dropped instances on some ranks the loss divisor (batch_num_tokens_for_loss) only counted unmasked tokens. With per-rank sum-then-allreduce, ranks with fewer kept tokens contributed an artificially large per-token loss, producing an unfair weighted average across the data-parallel group and a wrong gradient magnitude.
records.invariant: Across DP ranks the loss divisor must equal the global batch token count (including masked-instance tokens accounted as zero loss) so each rank contributes proportionally.

records.title: BLT distill metric not divided by num_micro_batches when grad_accum_steps>1
records.root_cause: batch_metrics accumulated detached metric tensors across micro-batches without dividing by num_micro_batches, so logged BLT decoder losses were inflated by the gradient accumulation factor while training itself proceeded normally.
records.invariant: Per-batch logged metrics should equal the average over micro-batches, not the sum.

records.title: SkipStepOptimizer fed unreduced ce_batch_loss — skip decisions on per-rank values
records.root_cause: SkipStepOptimizer.latest_loss was set from the local per-rank ce_batch_loss before the all-reduce that produced the global mean. The rolling-window statistics for outlier detection were thus computed on per-rank loss values, and skip-step decisions diverged across ranks, producing inconsistent optimizer behavior.
records.invariant: SkipStepOptimizer.latest_loss must be the globally reduced loss; all DP ranks must agree on whether to skip or not.

records.title: FlashAttn sliding-window off-by-one — window included one too many tokens
records.root_cause: Attention.__init__ stored self.window_size = (window_size, 0) when configuring sliding-window attention. Flash-attention's window is closed-interval [i - window_size[0], i + window_size[1]], so passing window_size directly let token i attend to window_size + 1 past tokens instead of window_size.
records.invariant: After configuration, the actual receptive window of each token under sliding attention must equal exactly the configured window_size positions.

records.title: Mamba2 ladder hard-coded head_dim from d_model/n_heads — wrong with FLA defaults
records.root_cause: The ladder configurators forced fla_layer_kwargs={'head_dim': ensure_multiple_of(d_model/n_heads, 128)}. FLA's Mamba2 already derives head_dim from its own internal layout, so injecting an externally-rounded value made the constructed Mamba2 layer disagree with the configured d_model/n_heads, producing a model whose effective head dimension differed from what other code assumed.
records.invariant: When using a third-party layer factory (FLA Mamba2), head_dim must be derived by that library, not externally rounded and re-injected.

records.title: BLT byte embeddings never initialized to teacher-embedding stats — kept default kaiming
records.root_cause: fix_init computed te_mean and te_std of the target embeddings but used them only when initializing hash_embeddings; the main self.embedding.weight (byte embeddings) was never assigned the te-scaled init, leaving it at nn.Embedding's default initialization. The encoder therefore started training with byte embeddings whose distribution did not match the teacher's vocabulary embeddings.
records.invariant: When a teacher embedding source is provided, the byte embedding must be sampled from a distribution with the same per-channel mean/std as the teacher embeddings.

records.title: TE attention backend silently ignored cu_doc_lens — intra-doc masking not applied
records.root_cause: TEAttentionBackend.forward accepted cu_doc_lens / max_doc_len arguments but did not pass them to TransformerEngine's attn kernel. Documents packed into a single sequence cross-attended each other instead of being masked at boundaries — full attention across all packed docs.
records.invariant: When cu_doc_lens is supplied, attention from token i must be limited to its own document; the TE backend must either honor cu_doc_lens or refuse the call.

records.title: Flex-attention sliding-window mask used Python `and` on tensors — short-circuit returned wrong mask
records.root_cause: _get_flex_attn_mask_mod._sliding_window_mask_mod returned `q_idx - kv_idx <= window_size[0] and kv_idx - q_idx <= window_size[1]`. Python's `and` calls bool() on the first operand and short-circuits — for scalar bool tensors this returns the second operand whenever the first is truthy and the first when falsy, never producing the intended logical AND. The mask was therefore computed as a single one-sided comparison.
records.invariant: Mask-mod functions for flex_attention must use torch.logical_and / & on tensors, never Python's `and`/`or`.

records.title: BLT stage1 froze only teacher.* — student blocks updated against teacher gradient
records.root_cause: freeze_params=['teacher.*'] only matched submodules named 'teacher.*'. Because share_blocks_between_teacher_and_student=True, the actual block parameters live under 'blocks.*' (shared with teacher); those weren't matched by the freeze pattern, so blocks were unfrozen and trained against gradients that included contributions from the teacher path.
records.invariant: freeze_params patterns must match every parameter that should remain frozen, including shared submodule names.

records.title: Document packing sort overflow — uint32 * -1 wraps to huge positive
freeze_experts assigned in __init__ instead of dataclass field — OmegaConf merge dropped it
records.root_cause: FreezeTransformerTrainModuleConfig set self.freeze_experts via kwargs.pop in __init__ rather than declaring it as a dataclass field. Config.merge serializes/reconstructs through OmegaConf, which drops fields that aren't declared dataclass attributes; freeze_experts always reverted to the default 'first_half' regardless of the user's configured value, silently zeroing the first half of router gradients.
records.invariant: Every user-tunable Config attribute must be a dataclass field so OmegaConf serialization preserves it through merge/dump.

records.title: MultiHeadLatentAttention init dispatched to Attention branch — wrong layers initialized
records.root_cause: InitMethod.init_attention dispatched on isinstance(m, Attention) before isinstance hasattr(m, 'wq_a'). Because MultiHeadLatentAttention inherits from Attention and exposes w_q, the MLA branch was never reached; the projections wq_a, wkv_a, wkv_b were never initialized while only w_q was, leaving the rest at the dtype-empty allocation values.
records.invariant: Every nn.Linear weight in attention sub-modules must be initialized exactly once via the appropriate init_attention branch before training starts.

records.title: Instance packing ladder set source_group_size on both Packing source and parent — double counting
records.root_cause: instance_packing_ladder set source_group_size=8 on both the inner NumpyDocumentSourceMixConfig and the outer PackingInstanceSourceConfig. The two interact multiplicatively in the source-permutation logic, so the effective grouping was 64 documents per group instead of the intended 8, changing the packing distribution silently.
records.invariant: source_group_size must be specified at exactly one layer of the source pipeline; duplicating it across nested configs changes the actual grouping by a multiplicative factor.

records.title: Qwen3Clone-8B script forgot use_head_qk_norm — used per-channel QK norm instead of per-head
records.root_cause: build_model_config for Qwen3Clone-8B configured the Qwen3 model but did not set config.block.attention.use_head_qk_norm = True. Qwen3 uses per-head QK norm; the default per-channel QK norm was applied instead, normalizing across the wrong axis and producing different attention scores from the reference Qwen3.
records.invariant: Model factories that clone HF reference models must set every option that affects forward semantics to match the reference, including use_head_qk_norm for Qwen3.

records.title: BLT debias used log(sum(exp(logprobs))) — silent underflow on small probabilities
records.root_cause: y_space_hat_all = log(einsum(exp(logprobs), space_mask).float()). exp() of low logprobs underflows to 0 in fp32, the masked sum collapses to 0, and log(0) = -inf is added into y_hat in-place. Subsequent loss terms silently propagate -inf values rather than failing.
records.invariant: All log-domain reductions should be performed via torch.logsumexp on a where-masked tensor instead of log(sum(exp(...))) over a multiplicative mask.

records.title: H-Net ratio loss averaged over padded positions — wrong target ratio under variable-length batches
records.root_cause: true_ratio = boundary_mask.float().mean() and average_prob = exp(boundary_logprobs).mean() averaged over the full padded byte tensor instead of over byte_mask-valid positions. Padded zero entries shrank both quantities toward 0, biasing the ratio loss target away from the true content ratio.
records.invariant: Any loss-target statistic over a variable-length sequence must be (x*mask).mean() / mask.mean(), not x.mean().

records.title: H-Net embed loss never normalized by loss_div_factor — wrong loss weighting
records.root_cause: The BLTDistillTransformer finalize block called self._finalize_loss on local_encoder_loss and local_decoder_loss but omitted the call for hnet_embed_loss. The component was added to the weighted-sum loss as a raw sum (not divided by token count), so its effective weight was inflated by approximately seq_len * batch_size relative to the configured loss_weights entry.
records.invariant: All loss components that appear in the weighted combination must be passed through _finalize_loss with the appropriate loss_div_factor.
