records.title: BLTDistill patch loss div factor used input_ids.numel() — wrong scaling for byte-level losses
records.root_cause: The byte-level loss div factor was computed as loss_div_factor / input_ids.numel(), but loss_div_factor passed in is at the byte sequence level not the patch level. The correct denominator is h_byte.shape[0] * h_byte.shape[1] (number of byte positions), and the patch loss needs an analogous division by patch positions. The mismatch silently mis-weighted byte vs patch loss components.
records.invariant: Each loss component must be divided by the number of valid positions of that component's granularity (bytes vs patches), not by input_ids.numel().

records.title: Flex attention not upcast to fp32 — precision mismatch with SDPA backend
records.root_cause: Flex attention was called directly on bf16 q/k/v while SDPA's reference path runs the matmul/softmax in fp32. The bf16-only flex path silently produced lower-precision attention outputs that diverge from the SDPA path used by tests, causing different loss trajectories between the two backends.
records.invariant: When flex_attention is the chosen backend, q/k/v must be upcast to fp32 inside an autocast(disabled) block to match SDPA's full-precision behavior, then the result cast back to og_dtype.

records.title: Sliding window size off-by-one — window 1 token too small
BLT distill missed first-call label_offsets when fuse_boundaries enabled
records.root_cause: The label-offset application path that conditionally adds vocab_size_blt to boundary positions was duplicated for the alternate boundary computation but missed in the first forward branch. Boundary positions did not get their offsets applied to labels, so the cross-entropy compared against the wrong target indices for boundary tokens.
records.invariant: When fuse_boundaries is enabled, every boundary position in labels must receive the +vocab_size_blt offset before being compared against the joint vocab logits.

records.title: BLT shift_boundary_mask did not AND with byte_mask — pad positions polluted label offsets
records.root_cause: shift_boundary_mask was computed as boundary_mask[:, 1:] without AND-ing with byte_mask[:, 1:]. Padded positions where boundary_mask happened to be True (left-over from a previous batch slot) added vocab_size_blt//2 to label entries that should have remained at the ignore_index, distorting CE on padded positions.
records.invariant: Any operation that mutates labels at boundary positions must restrict its mask via AND with the active byte_mask so padded positions are untouched.

records.title: SourceMixtureDataset rounded down per-source instances — dataset shorter than expected
records.root_cause: tokens_requested_per_path = ceil(target_ratio * num_tokens_in_path) and instances_requested_per_path = tokens_requested_per_path // sequence_length. The integer-floor in the second step dropped the per-path remainder, so total instances < training_steps * batch_size. The trainer ran past the end of the dataset into epoch 2 with no warning — visible only as an unexpected loss drop near end of run.
records.invariant: sum(instances_per_path) must equal training_steps * batch_size; any rounding-down must be redistributed (e.g. via Hamilton's largest-remainder method) so the trainer never wraps to epoch 2.

records.title: FSLDataset fingerprint missed sequence_length / bos_token_id — wrong cache reused
records.root_cause: fingerprint_fields for several FSLDataset variants did not include sequence_length, bos_token_id, max_target_sequence_length. Cached instance offsets / packed indices computed under the previous values were reused when those settings changed, so the dataset returned instances whose actual layout no longer matched the configured sequence_length.
records.invariant: Every dataset attribute that influences the on-disk cache layout must appear in fingerprint_fields so a config change invalidates the cache.

records.title: DataCollator routed academic/technical sources to a non-existent 4th expert label
records.root_cause: _source_name_to_expert_label produced a one-hot at index 3 for academic/technical sources, but the deployed model only had 3 active experts (indices 0..2 plus a masked duplicate). The label tensor pointed to an unused expert slot, so router supervision was silently directed to a slot the router never produced gradient for.
records.invariant: Expert label one-hot indices must lie within the active expert range of the model; 'general' must subsume any source not assigned to a specialized expert.

records.title: Attention gate w_g never initialized — uses uninitialized memory
records.root_cause: init_attention initialized w_q/w_k/w_v (and w_qkv for FusedAttention) but never touched the optional gate projection w_g. When constructed via nn.Linear with init_device='meta'/'cpu', w_g.weight held whatever values reset_parameters or torch.empty produced rather than the intended trunc-normal distribution.
records.invariant: Every learnable Linear weight in attention (including the optional gate projection) must be initialized exactly once via _init_linear before training starts.

records.title: InvSqrt LR schedule wrong scheduler chosen for OLMoE3 — Cos used where WSD intended
records.root_cause: OLMoE3-3B-27B used CosWithWarmup with only warmup_steps configured. Without an explicit decay schedule the optimizer ran cosine decay from peak lr to alpha_f over the full training horizon, instead of the WSD (warmup-stable-decay) schedule the recipe intended. The lr trajectory was silently cosine-shaped instead of WSD-shaped.
records.invariant: WSD-style training recipes must use the WSD scheduler with explicit warmup, decay step counts, and decay_fraction=None — not CosWithWarmup, even though both yield monotonic lr curves.

records.title: soft_target_probs silently truncated to int by custom as_tensor
PoE z_loss combined into combined_loss is detached, contributing value but no gradient
records.root_cause: In TransformerTrainModule.train_batch the PoE branch added output.z_loss to combined_loss, but LMHead emits output.z_loss as a detached metric tensor. The optimizer therefore saw the z_loss value in the printed metric while backprop applied zero z_loss gradient, so logit-norm regularization never actually constrained the weights.
records.invariant: Any tensor summed into combined_loss prior to backward() must have requires_grad=True so the regularizer reaches the parameters.

records.title: soft_ce branch backprops only alpha*soft_ce — hard_ce gradient zeroed because output.ce_loss is detached
records.root_cause: The soft-CE branch built combined_loss = (1-alpha)*hard_ce_loss + alpha*soft_ce_loss + z_loss using output.ce_loss and output.z_loss, both of which LMHead returns as .detach()'d copies. Only output.loss carries gradient. As soon as alpha decayed to 0 the entire backward() saw zero gradient and grad_norm collapsed.
records.invariant: grad_norm must remain positive when (1-alpha) > 0; the (1-alpha) coefficient on hard CE must contribute non-zero parameter gradient.
